project: SHF GMO Likelihood Detection & Lookup Architecture
version: 0.1 — draft, pending Non-GMO Project / USDA BE list cross-reference
scope_note: Likelihood only, never proof — a photo cannot confirm GMO content, only flag evidence. This constraint is a UI requirement as much as a data one: every verdict screen must state it plainly.

certification_short_circuit.note: Check BEFORE ingredient matching, same pattern as fluoride's organic-cert short circuit. A certification is stronger evidence than any ingredient match.

explicit_crop_matches.note: Ingredient directly names a high-GMO-adoption crop. Strong evidence — these are what count toward the likelihood score.

entries.note: Hawaiian papaya specifically — high GMO adoption due to ringspot virus resistance breeding

ambiguous_derivative_matches.note: Common ingredients that MAY derive from a GMO crop but the label does not disclose the source. Presence of these should lower confidence, not raise likelihood — this is the key difference from fluoride matching.

possible_sources: palm — cannot determine without further label detail

likelihood_scoring.method: Count N = number of DISTINCT crop_family values matched from explicit_crop_matches only. Ambiguous derivatives never count toward N.
likelihood_scoring.rationale: Distinct families, not raw ingredient count — 'corn syrup, corn starch, modified corn starch' is still just corn (N=1), not High. Prevents single-crop products from over-scoring.

confidence_scoring.method: Points system, same shape as fluoride's confidence formula.

factors.condition: Full list OCR'd, no visible truncation
Barcode/name matched an Open Food Facts entry
≥80% of extracted ingredients recognized (matched explicit crop, ambiguous derivative, or known non-GMO-relevant ingredient)
Cert statement clearly readable either way (has one, or explicitly none)
One or more ambiguous derivatives matched with NO explicit crop match found elsewhere
factors.note: This is the GMO-specific addition — reflects that the evidence is genuinely inconclusive, not just incomplete

fields.ui: Low / Medium / High GMO Likelihood — primary badge
secondary badge, always shown alongside Result

fields.from: terms_lookup_table matches found in ingredients text

fields.note: Only shown if a certification was detected
Must always restate the honesty constraint: a photo estimates likelihood from visible evidence, it cannot confirm GMO content — this line is non-negotiable per the brief

submission_form_schema.note: Same trigger logic as fluoride — shown when confidence is Low. Mirrors fluoride form shape.

fields.field: Certification visible on packaging, if any
fields.input: dropdown from certification_short_circuit terms, or 'none visible'

open_questions_before_v1: Cross-reference explicit_crop_matches and ambiguous_derivative_matches against the Non-GMO Project's published High-Risk Ingredients list and the USDA Bioengineered Food List — this draft is a starting seed, not verified against those sources yet

Decide whether Open Food Facts ingredient tags (e.g. en:corn-starch) can be matched directly instead of building custom text normalization — worth a spike before committing dev time to a regex-based parser
Confirm whether zucchini/summer squash (also GM-adopted in some markets) is relevant given your target shelf, or safely out of scope
